summary: Phase 21 (Prime Lemma 5.3.1 at 𝒯 = ∅) is BLOCKED: its deliverable is not constructible as specified. TPrime 𝒯 Atom is UNINHABITED for EVERY 𝒯, including 𝒯 = ∅ -- mechanized sorry-free as tPrime_false / instance IsEmpty (TPrime 𝒯 Atom). Lemma 5.3.1's whole job is to PRODUCE an inhabitant of that type, so no proof effort at any 𝒯 can succeed until it is repaired. This SUPERSEDES Phase 20's scoping, which found the emptiness only at TS5, attributed it to χ_T's quantifier range, and concluded it 'lands on Phase 23, not Phase 21' and that plan v3's D2 '𝒯 = ∅ first' sequencing 'independently saves Phase 21'. Clause 0 IS vacuous at ∅ -- but clause 1 (deductiveClosure) empties the type on its own, independently of 𝒯: NIK.impI + NIK.assumption derive x : A ⊃ A at an ARBITRARY label, over an arbitrary graph, from the EMPTY assumption list, with no premises and no side conditions (and, as Phase 20 itself established, NIK never reads G.X at all). Type-wide deductiveClosure then forces (x : A⊃A) ∈ Γ for every label, Context.ctxSubset forces G.X = univ, and Context.coinfinite contradicts it. The 𝒯 = ∅ route does not dodge the emptiness. Reading Simpson's Figure 4-1 from the p. 69 page RASTER (its pdftotext layer is destroyed -- the same text-layer failure mode Phase 20 documented for H_i on p. 92) surfaced two FURTHER transcription defects: (⊥E) is printed CROSS-LABEL (x:⊥ / y:A) but transcribed label-local as NIK.efq, and (∨E) is printed CROSS-LABEL (major premise x:A∨B, conclusion y:C) but transcribed label-local as NIK.orE. Those are precisely the two rules Lemma 5.3.1 uses to discharge consistency and the disjunction property, and both transcriptions are STRICT WEAKENINGS (mechanized: the printed rules imply CSLib's). All three defects, plus Phase 20's clModel finding, share ONE root cause: the transcription drops the domain-relativity / cross-label structure Simpson's Chapter 5 relies on. Declarations landed (probes/prime-lemma-blockers.lean, 11 decls, sorry-free, axioms ⊆ [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]): NIK.imp_self, Deriv.imp_self, tPrime_false, instIsEmptyTPrime, deductiveClosure_relativized_kills_the_chain, EfqCrossLabel, consistency_of_efqCrossLabel, consistency_at_excluded_label_only, efq_of_efqCrossLabel, OrECrossLabel, orE_labelLocal_of_orECrossLabel. Cslib/ untouched (git status --short Cslib/ empty). No sorries planted -- nothing was attempted against a provably empty type. The ROUTE is not what failed: p. 92 confirms the Zorn-over-whole-contexts construction verbatim.

blockers.title: TPrime 𝒯 Atom is uninhabited for every 𝒯, including 𝒯 = ∅
blockers.what_failed: Phase 21's deliverable -- a 𝒯-prime context -- cannot exist. The target type is empty at every 𝒯.
blockers.what_was_tried: Transcribed Lemma 5.3.1 from the PDF rasters (pp. 92-93), then ran the dispatch's mandated small-model/consistency check on the STATEMENT before writing the Zorn argument. The check failed the type itself, so the Zorn argument was never started.
blockers.root_cause: TPrime.deductiveClosure (Context.lean:219) is typed `∀ (x : Label Atom) (A : Proposition Atom), Deriv 𝒯 G Γ (x ∶ A) → (x ∶ A) ∈ Γ` -- a TYPE-WIDE quantifier over labels. But NIK.impI + NIK.assumption derive (x ∶ A ⊃ A) at an arbitrary label from the empty list with no side conditions, and NIK never reads G.X. So deductiveClosure forces (x ∶ A⊃A) ∈ Γ for every label x; ctxSubset forces x ∈ G.X for every x (G.X = univ); coinfinite supplies Label.var n with n ∉ V'. Contradiction. Simpson's clause 1 (p. 92) reads 'If Γ ⊢^𝒯_G x:A then x:A ∈ Γ' where ⊢_G is a judgement about labels OF G; Lemma 5.3.2 (p. 94) makes the same domain-relativity explicit in its own statement ('for all y IN H'). The type-wide reading is a transcription defect.
blockers.what_is_needed: Relativize clause 1 in Cslib/Logics/Modal/Metalogic/Constructive/Labelled/Context.lean:219 to `deductiveClosure : ∀ x ∈ G.X, ∀ A, Deriv 𝒯 G Γ (x ∶ A) → (x ∶ A) ∈ Γ`. Adequacy checked in the probe. This is not merely a strength question: the relativized clause is exactly what Lemma 5.3.1's OWN deductive-closure step needs -- Simpson forms the context (H, Δ ∪ {y:B}), whose Context.ctxSubset obligation demands y ∈ H.X, which only the relativized clause supplies as a hypothesis. The type-wide clause is unusable at the very step that consumes it.
blockers.supersedes: Phase 20's tPrime_TS5_false scoping. Phase 20's IsEmpty (TPrime TS5 Atom) is a special case of tPrime_false. Phase 20's conclusion that the emptiness 'lands on Phase 23, not Phase 21' and that D2's sequencing 'independently saves Phase 21 from a blocker nobody had spotted' is FALSE.

blockers.title: (⊥E) transcribed label-local; Simpson's Figure 4-1 prints it cross-label
blockers.what_failed: Lemma 5.3.1's consistency clause cannot be discharged the way Simpson discharges it.
blockers.root_cause: Simpson Figure 4-1 (p. 69, PDF p. 78, read from the page RASTER) prints `x:⊥ / y:A` -- premise and conclusion at DIFFERENT labels. CSLib's NIK.efq (Deduction.lean) is `x:⊥ / x:A`, label-local, and its docstring says so explicitly. Lemma 5.3.1's 'Consistency is immediate, because Δ ⊬^𝒯_H x:A' (p. 93) bridges y:⊥ to x:A ACROSS the label boundary; only the cross-label rule does that, and nothing else in the system does. Note the argument needs no maximality -- it is a property of any context avoiding x:A, exactly as Simpson says.
blockers.what_is_needed: Retype NIK.efq to Figure 4-1's form: `| efq (G) (Γ) (x y) (A) (h : NIK 𝒯 G Γ (x ∶ .bot)) : NIK 𝒯 G Γ (y ∶ A)`. SOUNDNESS RE-CHECK REQUIRED and NOT done in this dispatch: semantically the cross-label rule looks fine (no interpretation makes ρ(x) ⊩ ⊥, so ρ(y) ⊩ A vacuously), but the landed CK/CT/CS4/CS5 soundness results and task-509's cs5FC'' must be re-verified against the strengthened rule. That verification is the repair's main risk and its precondition.
blockers.territory_note: Repair is in Cslib/, out of Phase 21's territory. Not applied.

blockers.title: (∨E) transcribed label-local; Simpson's Figure 4-1 prints it cross-label
blockers.what_failed: Lemma 5.3.1's disjunction-property clause cannot be discharged the way Simpson discharges it.
blockers.root_cause: Simpson Figure 4-1 (p. 69, PDF p. 78, raster) prints major premise `x:A∨B`, minor premises `y:C` under discharged `[x:A]`/`[x:B]`, conclusion `y:C` -- the disjunction's label is INDEPENDENT of the conclusion's. CSLib's NIK.orE fixes all of them at x ('label-local case split'). Lemma 5.3.1 (p. 93) argues: 'suppose that y:B ∨ C ∈ Δ. Now either Δ,y:B ⊬^𝒯_H x:A or Δ,y:C ⊬^𝒯_H x:A, for otherwise we would have that Δ ⊢^𝒯_H x:A by an application of (∨E)' -- disjunction at y, derived formula at x. Under the label-local rule that application is ill-formed, so the clause is dischargeable only for disjunctions sitting at the excluded label x.
blockers.what_is_needed: Retype NIK.orE to Figure 4-1's form: `| orE (G) (Γ) (x y) (A B C) (hor : NIK 𝒯 G Γ (x ∶ .or A B)) (hA : NIK 𝒯 G ((x ∶ A) :: Γ) (y ∶ C)) (hB : NIK 𝒯 G ((x ∶ B) :: Γ) (y ∶ C)) : NIK 𝒯 G Γ (y ∶ C)`. Same soundness re-check requirement as the efq repair; not done here.
blockers.territory_note: Repair is in Cslib/, out of Phase 21's territory. Not applied.

blockers.title: Simpson's chain-union step may not transfer to CSLib's cofinite-quantification encoding -- the real crux
blockers.root_cause: Simpson's Zorn step says 'It is easily seen that (⋃_{i∈I} G_i, ⋃_{i∈I} Γ_i) is also in C' (p. 92). That needs: Deriv 𝒯 G_∞ Γ_∞ (x∶A) → ∃ i, Deriv 𝒯 G_i Γ_i (x∶A) -- a finite-support argument. But NIK.boxI and NIK.diaE encode their eigenvariable side-condition by COFINITE QUANTIFICATION (∀ y ∉ L, L finite), so a NIK derivation has INFINITE BRANCHING and no finite graph support: rebuilding a boxI at a single chain index i requires ONE i valid for cofinitely many y, and directedness does not supply it (each y yields its own i_y, unboundedly). Simpson's own derivations are finite trees with ONE eigenvariable premise -- which is why he calls the step 'easily seen'. The gap is created by the encoding, not by the mathematics.
blockers.what_is_needed: Almost certainly a label-renaming / equivariance lemma for NIK (if NIK 𝒯 (G.addEdge x y) Γ₀ (y∶A) for one fresh y, then for every fresh y'), letting one index i transport across all eigenvariables. No such lemma exists in Cslib/. A successor MUST settle this BEFORE attempting the Zorn argument -- it is upstream of the whole construction.
blockers.supersedes: Phase 20 rated this LOW uncertainty ('the union of a chain of contexts is genuinely routine'), judging it from signatures + Deriv.mono without mechanizing it. That rating looks optimistic: Deriv.mono is monotonicity (the easy direction); the chain step needs the REFLECTION direction, which is where the cofinite encoding bites.
